newsitem.title: KENYA: Foreign demand push Nairobi bourse blue chips up.
newsitem.headline: Foreign demand push Nairobi bourse blue chips up.

text.p: Increased foreign participation at the Nairobi Stock Exchange (NSE) helped its 20-share index make further gains riding on increased prices in blue-chip shares.
In what brokers described as a continuous trading session, the NSE index went up 22.18 points to close at 3512.99.
Turnover was posted at 26.7 million shillings compared to 41.6 million shillings on Tuesday. Total shares traded were 1,561,868 from 747,025.
Local bank Kenya Commercial Bank and Kenya Power & Lighting are the main buying focus for foreign investors, the only problem being that they are few in the market, brokers said.
A broker from a leading brokerage firm told Reuters that they were getting a lot of positive feedback from foreign fund managers.
"A lot of them feel that with the continued reforms, Kenya's economic fundamentals are finally falling into place and it has become attractive, even to other African markets," he said.
They said the power monopoly especially had generated a lot of interest from investors, both local and foreign because of the promise of future capitalisation issues.
Foreign investors traded Kenya Power & Lighting at between 170 and 176 from 170, Kenya Airways at 9.50 from 8.25 and National Industrial Credit Bank at 57-58 from 57.
Among plantations Brooke Bond closed at 123 from 122 while George Williamson eased to 70 from 71. Limuru Tea traded at 1000 from 1300 while Rea Vipingo Plantations closed at 9.10 from 9.
Uchumi Supermarket edged to 39 from 38.25 while Nation Printers & Publishers eased to 112 from 115.
Kenya Breweries closed at 57.50 from 57 while Total Kenya eased to 64 from 65.
The Central Bank of Kenya floating rate treasury bond traded 3.25 million shillings at 100.3149 percent from 100.1586 percent.
